meta.title: Volleyball Rules Quiz
meta.description: Test your knowledge of volleyball rules based on the FIVB Official Volleyball Rules 2025-2028.
meta.disclaimer: This quiz is for educational purposes. It is not affiliated with or endorsed by the FIVB. Rule references are based on the FIVB Official Volleyball Rules 2025-2028.

questions.question: What is the official net height for men's volleyball?
questions.explanation: The net height for men is 2.43 m, measured from the centre of the playing court.

questions.question: What is the official net height for women's volleyball?
questions.explanation: The net height for women is 2.24 m, measured from the centre of the playing court.

questions.question: What are the dimensions of a volleyball court?
questions.explanation: The playing court is a rectangle measuring 18 x 9 m.

questions.question: How many players per team are on the court during play?
questions.explanation: There must always be six players per team in play.

questions.question: How many players can a team register on the score sheet for a standard match?
questions.explanation: A team may consist of up to 12 players. For FIVB Senior competitions, up to 14 players may be recorded.

questions.question: How many liberos can a team designate?
questions.explanation: Each team has the right to designate up to two specialist defensive players: Liberos.

questions.question: In FIVB Senior competitions, if a team has more than 12 players on the score sheet, having two liberos is mandatory.
questions.explanation: For FIVB Senior competitions, if a team has more than 12 players recorded on the score sheet, two liberos are mandatory.

questions.question: How many substitutions is a team allowed per set?
questions.explanation: Each team may request a maximum of six substitutions per set.

questions.question: How many time-outs is each team allowed per set?
questions.explanation: Each team may request a maximum of two time-outs per set.

questions.question: How long does a requested time-out last?
questions.explanation: All requested time-outs last for 30 seconds.

questions.question: How many points are needed to win a regular set (not the deciding set)?
questions.explanation: A set (except the deciding 5th set) is won by the team which first scores 25 points with a minimum lead of two points.

questions.question: How many points are needed to win the deciding 5th set?
questions.explanation: The deciding 5th set is played to 15 points with a minimum lead of 2 points.

questions.question: How many sets does a team need to win to win the match?
questions.explanation: The match is won by the team that wins three sets (best of five).

questions.question: The ball can be played with any part of the body.
questions.explanation: The ball may touch any part of the body. There is no restriction on which body part can contact the ball.

questions.question: On the first hit of the team (such as a receive or dig), the ball can touch multiple body parts in sequence as long as it happens in one continuous action.
questions.explanation: At the first hit of the team, the ball may contact various parts of the body consecutively, provided that the contacts occur during one action. For example, the ball hitting the forearm and then rolling up to the shoulder on a dig is legal if it's one motion.

questions.question: On the second or third hit of the team, the ball can touch multiple body parts in sequence (one after another) during the contact.
questions.explanation: On the second or third hit, the ball may only touch various parts of the body if the contacts take place simultaneously. Consecutive (sequential) contacts are only allowed on the first hit of the team or during a block.

questions.question: If the ball lands on a boundary line, it is considered 'in'.
questions.explanation: The ball is 'in' if at any moment of its contact with the floor, some part of the ball touches the court, including the boundary lines.

questions.question: A player who touches the net between the antennae during the action of playing the ball commits a fault.
questions.explanation: Contact with the net by a player between the antennae, during the action of playing the ball, is a fault. The action of playing the ball includes take-off, hit (or attempt), and landing.

questions.question: Touching the net outside the antennae is always a fault.
questions.explanation: Touching the net outside the antennae is NOT a fault. Players may touch the post, ropes, or any other object outside the antennae, including the net itself, provided that it does not interfere with play.

questions.question: A player steps on the centre line with one foot during play. The other foot remains on their own side. Is this allowed?
options: No, any contact with the centre line is a fault
Yes, as long as some part of the foot remains on or directly above the centre line
Yes, players can freely cross the centre line
Only the libero is allowed to step on the centre line
questions.explanation: Touching the opponent's court with a foot is permitted, provided that some part of the penetrating foot remains either in contact with or directly above the centre line.

questions.question: If a player's foot completely crosses the centre line and lands entirely on the opponent's court, it is a fault.
questions.explanation: A player's foot (or feet) penetrating completely into the opponent's court is a fault. Some part of the foot must remain on or above the centre line.

questions.question: What about body parts above the feet crossing the centre line? For example, a player's hand touches the opponent's court floor.
options: Permitted as long as it does not interfere with the opponent's play
Only the arms are allowed to cross
questions.explanation: Touching the opponent's court with any part of the body above the feet is permitted, provided that it does not interfere with the opponent's play.

questions.question: It is legal to block the opponent's serve.
questions.explanation: Blocking the opponent's service is forbidden.

questions.question: A block contact counts as one of the team's three hits.
questions.explanation: A block contact is NOT counted as a team hit. After a block contact, a team is still entitled to three hits to return the ball.

questions.question: A player touches the ball during a block. How many more hits does the team get?
options: 0 — the block was their first hit
questions.explanation: A block contact is not counted as a team hit. After a block, the team is entitled to three more hits to return the ball. The blocker can even make the first of those three hits.

questions.question: Only front-row players are allowed to complete a block.
questions.explanation: Only front-row players are permitted to complete a block. Back-row players and the libero cannot block or participate in a completed block.

questions.question: A back-row player wants to attack the ball. Where must they take off from if the ball is entirely above the net?
questions.explanation: A back-row player may complete an attack hit at any height from behind the front zone. At take-off, the player's foot must not have touched or crossed the attack line.

questions.question: After a back-row attack, the player is allowed to land inside the front zone (in front of the attack line).
questions.explanation: After the hit, the back-row player may land within the front zone. The restriction only applies at the moment of take-off.

questions.question: A back-row player standing inside the front zone can attack the ball if part of the ball is below the top of the net at the moment of contact.
questions.explanation: A back-row player may complete an attack hit from the front zone, if at the moment of contact a part of the ball is lower than the top of the net.

questions.question: How many seconds does the server have to hit the ball after the referee's whistle?
questions.explanation: The server must hit the ball within 8 seconds after the 1st referee whistles for service.

questions.question: At the moment of serving, the server's foot touches the end line. What happens?
options: Nothing, touching the line is allowed
It is a foot fault — service fault
The referee gives a warning first
questions.explanation: At the moment of the service hit (or take-off for a jump serve), the server must not touch the court, including the end line, or the floor outside the service zone.

questions.question: After hitting the serve, the server is allowed to step on the court or land inside the playing area.
questions.explanation: After the service hit, the server may step or land outside the service zone or inside the court. The restriction only applies at the moment of the hit or take-off.

questions.question: What is the maximum number of hits a team can use to return the ball (not counting a block)?
questions.explanation: The team is entitled to a maximum of three hits (in addition to blocking) for returning the ball.

questions.question: Which of the following is the libero NOT allowed to do?
options: Dig a ball in the back row
Serve, block, or attempt to block
questions.explanation: The libero may not serve, block, or attempt to block. They can do everything else as a back-row player, including digging and passing.

questions.question: The libero can attack the ball as long as it is entirely above the net at the moment of contact.
questions.explanation: The libero is NOT allowed to complete an attack hit if the ball is entirely higher than the top of the net at the moment of contact. This applies from anywhere on the court, including the free zone.

questions.question: The libero sets the ball using an overhand finger pass while standing inside the front zone. What restriction applies?
options: No restriction — the set is legal and anyone can attack it
The set is a fault and play stops immediately
No teammate may attack that ball above net height
Only the middle blocker can attack the ball
questions.explanation: If the libero sets the ball using an overhand finger pass from the front zone, no teammate may complete an attack hit when the ball is entirely above the top of the net. The libero CAN make the set — it is the attack that becomes restricted.

questions.question: If the libero sets the ball with an overhand finger pass from behind the attack line (back zone), the attack restriction does not apply.
questions.explanation: The ball may be freely attacked if the libero makes the overhand finger pass from outside the front zone. The restriction only applies when the libero is in the front zone.

questions.question: Libero replacements count against the team's six substitutions per set.
questions.explanation: Libero replacements are NOT counted as substitutions. They are unlimited, but there must be a completed rally between two libero replacements.

questions.question: How many liberos can be on the court at the same time?
questions.explanation: Only one libero may be on the court at any time, even if the team has designated two liberos.

questions.question: The libero can replace which type of player?
questions.explanation: The libero is allowed to replace any player in a back-row position. In practice, teams most commonly replace the middle blocker in the back row, but the rules allow replacement of any back-row player.

questions.question: What colour jersey must the libero wear?
options: A different dominant colour that clearly contrasts with the rest of the team
questions.explanation: The libero must wear a uniform with a different dominant colour from any colour of the rest of the team, and it must clearly contrast with the rest of the team.

questions.question: The ball is allowed to touch the net while crossing over to the opponent's side.
questions.explanation: While crossing the net, the ball may touch it. A ball touching the net is not a fault.

questions.question: A serve that touches the net and goes over to the opponent's side is a fault.
questions.explanation: The ball may touch the net while crossing, including on a serve. As long as the ball crosses the net within the crossing space and lands in the opponent's court, it is legal. The old 'let serve' rule was removed long ago.

questions.question: Players of the serving team are allowed to raise their hands above their heads during service to block the opponent's view.
questions.explanation: Any player of the serving team is forbidden to raise hands above the head during service until the ball has passed beyond the net. This is part of the screening rules.

questions.question: How far is the attack line from the centre line?
questions.explanation: The attack line is drawn 3 m back from the axis of the centre line. It marks the boundary of the front zone.

questions.question: What is the standard interval (break) between sets?
questions.explanation: All intervals between sets last three minutes. The interval between the 2nd and 3rd set can be extended up to 10 minutes by the organizer.

questions.question: Teams change sides of the court after every set.
questions.explanation: After each set, the teams change courts, with the exception of the deciding set where teams change when the leading team reaches 8 points.

questions.question: In the deciding 5th set, when do the teams change sides of the court?
options: They don't change sides in the 5th set
questions.explanation: In the deciding set, once the leading team reaches 8 points, the teams change courts without delay and the player positions remain the same.

questions.question: A starting player is substituted out. Can they come back into the game in the same set?
options: No, once substituted out they are out for the set
Yes, but only once and only to their original position
Yes, they can re-enter as many times as needed
Only if the team has remaining substitutions
questions.explanation: A player of the starting line-up may leave the game but only once in a set, and re-enter but only once in a set, and only to their previous position in the line-up.

questions.question: Player A (starter) is substituted by Player B. Who can substitute Player B back out?
options: Player B cannot be substituted out
questions.explanation: A substitute player may enter the game in place of a starting player, but only once per set, and they can only be substituted by the same starting player who they replaced.

questions.question: When the ball is driven into the net and the net touches an opponent player, it is a fault on that opponent.
questions.explanation: When the ball is driven into the net, causing it to touch an opponent, no fault is committed. The net contact was caused by the ball, not by the player's action.

questions.question: During a block, the ball can make consecutive contacts with one or more blockers and it is still legal.
questions.explanation: Consecutive (quick and continuous) contacts with the ball may occur by one or more blockers, provided that the contacts are made during one action.

questions.question: Two opponents touch the ball simultaneously over the net. The ball stays in play and lands on Team A's side. How many hits does Team A get?
questions.explanation: When two opponents touch the ball simultaneously over the net and the ball remains in play, the team receiving the ball is entitled to another three hits.

questions.question: What number range must players' jerseys be numbered in?
questions.explanation: Players' jerseys must be numbered from 1 to 20. In FIVB Senior competitions with larger squads, numbers may be extended.

questions.question: A player is allowed to hold or catch the ball briefly before directing it to a teammate.
questions.explanation: The ball must not be caught and/or thrown. It can rebound in any direction, but it must not come to rest in a player's hands.

questions.question: How wide are the court lines?
questions.explanation: All lines on the court are 5 cm wide.

questions.question: A player who is about to touch the net can be stopped or held back by a teammate without it being a fault.
questions.explanation: A player who is about to commit a fault (such as touching the net or crossing the centre line) may be stopped or held back by a teammate. This is an exception to the assisted hit rule.

questions.question: The score is 24-24 in the 4th set. What happens?
options: The set goes to a tie-break
Play continues until one team leads by 2 points
The next point wins the set
The set is declared a draw
questions.explanation: In the case of a 24-24 tie, play is continued until a two-point lead is achieved (26-24, 27-25, etc.). There is no cap.

questions.question: The service can be executed with a closed fist, an open hand, or any part of the arm.
questions.explanation: The ball shall be hit with one hand or any part of the arm after being tossed or released from the hand(s). There is no restriction on using a fist versus an open hand.

questions.question: A team member holds a teammate up by the shoulders so they can reach a high ball. Is this legal?
options: No, this is an assisted hit fault
Only if the teammate is the libero
questions.explanation: Within the playing area, a player is not permitted to take support from a teammate or any structure/object in order to hit the ball. This is called an assisted hit fault.

questions.question: What happens if two faults are committed by the same team one after the other during a rally?
options: Only the first fault is counted
Only the more severe fault is counted
questions.explanation: If two or more faults are committed successively, only the first one is counted.

questions.question: What happens when both teams commit a fault at the same time (simultaneously)?
options: The serving team wins the point
The receiving team wins the point
A double fault is called and the rally is replayed
The referee decides which fault was more severe
questions.explanation: If two or more faults are committed by opponents simultaneously, a double fault is called and the rally is replayed.

questions.question: In blocking, a player reaches over the net into the opponent's space. When is this allowed?
options: Never — you cannot reach over the net
Only if the ball has already crossed to your side
Only after the opponent's attack hit
At any time, as long as it does not interfere with the opponent's play before their attack hit
questions.explanation: In blocking, a player may touch the ball beyond the net, provided that they do not interfere with the opponent's play before the opponent's attack hit.

questions.question: There must be a completed rally between two libero replacements.
questions.explanation: Libero replacements are unlimited but there must be a completed rally between two libero replacements.

questions.question: The server tosses the ball for a serve but decides not to hit it. What happens?
options: The server can re-toss freely — there is no limit
It is a service fault — the opponent wins the point
The server can catch the ball and re-toss once
This is not covered in the rules
questions.explanation: Only one toss or release of the ball is allowed for a serve. If the server tosses the ball and does not hit it, it is a service fault and the opponent wins the point.

questions.question: At the moment the server contacts the ball, which team must be in the correct rotational positions?
options: Neither team — positions only matter after the serve
questions.explanation: The players of the receiving team must be in the rotational order at the service hit. The players of the serving team are free to occupy any position at the service hit.

questions.question: The serving team must follow overlap (positional) rules at the moment of serve.
questions.explanation: The players of the serving team are free to occupy any position at the service hit. Only the receiving team must be in the correct rotational order.

questions.question: How are player positions determined for checking overlap (positional) rules?
options: By the position of their torso
By the position of their feet contacting the ground
By where the referee estimates they are standing
questions.explanation: The positions of players are determined and controlled according to the positions of their feet contacting the ground. The last contact with the floor fixes the player's position.

questions.question: For overlap rules: the player in zone 4 (front-left) must be positioned in front of which player?
questions.explanation: Each front-row player must be closer to the net than the corresponding back-row player. Zone 4 (front-left) corresponds to zone 5 (back-left).

questions.question: For overlap rules: the player in zone 3 (front-centre) must be positioned in front of which player?
questions.explanation: Zone 3 (front-centre) must be closer to the net than zone 6 (back-centre). Each front-row player is paired with the back-row player directly behind them.

questions.question: In the front row, zone 4 must be to the left of zone 3, and zone 3 must be to the left of zone 2.
questions.explanation: The front-row and back-row players must be positioned laterally in the correct order. In the front row: zone 4 (left) must be left of zone 3 (centre), and zone 3 must be left of zone 2 (right).

questions.question: After the server contacts the ball, players on both teams can move anywhere on the court.
questions.explanation: After the service hit, the players of both teams may move around and occupy any position on their court and the free zone.

questions.question: When a team wins back the right to serve (side-out), in which direction do the players rotate?
options: They don't rotate — only the server changes
questions.explanation: When the receiving team gains the right to serve, its players rotate one position clockwise.

questions.question: After a rotation, which player goes to position 1 (back-right) to serve?
questions.explanation: The player in position 2 rotates to position 1 to serve. The player in position 1 rotates to position 6, and so on clockwise.

questions.question: Which zones are considered the front row?
questions.explanation: The three front-row positions are zone 4 (front-left), zone 3 (front-centre), and zone 2 (front-right). The back row consists of zones 5, 6, and 1.

questions.question: Which zones are considered the back row?
questions.explanation: The three back-row positions are zone 5 (back-left), zone 6 (back-centre), and zone 1 (back-right).

questions.question: What is the penalty for a positional fault (overlap violation)?
options: Point and service to the opponent
Yellow card to the player out of position
questions.explanation: A positional fault leads to the team being sanctioned with a point and service to the opponent, and the players' positions must be corrected.

questions.question: For overlap rules, each player only needs to maintain their position relative to adjacent neighbours — not diagonally opposite players.
questions.explanation: Players only need to maintain correct positioning relative to their adjacent neighbours in the same row (left-right) and their corresponding front/back partner. There is no diagonal constraint. For example, the zone 4 player does not need to be left of the zone 2 player.

questions.question: If two players in the same row are exactly level (aligned), this counts as a positional fault.
questions.explanation: Being 'level with' (exactly aligned) is legal. Each player needs at least a part of one foot in the correct relative position — being level satisfies this requirement.

questions.question: The rotational order set at the beginning of a set can be changed during that set.
questions.explanation: The team's starting line-up indicates the rotational order of the players on the court. This order must be maintained throughout the set.

questions.question: Zone numbering starts at which position on the court?
questions.explanation: Zone 1 is at the back-right of the court, which is the serving position. Numbering continues counter-clockwise: zone 2 (front-right), zone 3 (front-centre), zone 4 (front-left), zone 5 (back-left), zone 6 (back-centre).

questions.question: Both the server and a receiving team player commit a fault at the moment of the serve. The server makes an improper serve, and a receiving player is out of position. Which fault is called?
questions.explanation: If the server makes a fault at the moment of the service hit and the opponent is out of position, it is the serving fault which is sanctioned.

questions.question: A serve is executed legally but then goes out of bounds. A receiving player was also out of position. Which fault is called?
options: The positional fault (it happened first, at the moment of serve)
questions.explanation: If the service execution was correct but the serve subsequently becomes faulty (goes out, etc.), the positional fault has taken place first (at the moment of the serve) and is sanctioned.

questions.question: Before the first set, what may the winner of the toss choose?
options: Either serve/receive or the side of the court
Only the side of the court
questions.explanation: The toss winner chooses either the right to serve or receive, or the side of the court. The other team gets the remaining choice.

questions.question: A new toss is held before the deciding 5th set.
questions.explanation: If a deciding set is played, a new toss is carried out before that set.

questions.question: If the teams did not have a court exclusively for warm-up before the match, how long is the official warm-up together at the net?
questions.explanation: If the teams did not previously have a court at their exclusive disposal, they are entitled to 10 minutes together at the net.

questions.question: All balls used in one match must have the same standards for size, weight, pressure, type, and colour.
questions.explanation: All balls used in a match must have the same standards.

questions.question: Players are allowed to wear objects that may cause injury or give an artificial advantage.
questions.explanation: Objects that may cause injury or give an artificial advantage are forbidden.

questions.question: When the ball is out of play, who is allowed to ask the referees for a rule explanation?
questions.explanation: When the ball is out of play, only the game captain is authorized to speak to the referees for clarification.

questions.question: If a team is declared incomplete, it keeps any points and sets it had already won.
questions.explanation: An incomplete team loses the set or match, but it keeps the points and sets it had already earned.

questions.question: A ball that touches the ceiling is out.
questions.explanation: The ball is out if it touches an object outside the court, including the ceiling.

questions.question: A ball that touches an antenna is out.
questions.explanation: The ball is out if it touches the antennae.

questions.question: A ball crosses partly or fully through the external space to the opponent free zone. When can the team still play it back?
options: Only if it came from the first team hit
Only if it came from the second team hit
Only if it came from a block
questions.explanation: A ball that goes through the external space may be played back only if it came from the first hit of the team.

questions.question: A ball driven into the net may still be recovered within the team's three hits.
questions.explanation: A ball driven into the net may be recovered as long as the team stays within its three hits.

questions.question: A serve hit before the referee's whistle is cancelled and repeated.
questions.explanation: A serve executed before the whistle is cancelled and replayed.

questions.question: During the serve, a player on the serving team may raise both hands above the head before the ball passes the net.
questions.explanation: Players on the serving team are forbidden to raise their hands above the head during service until the ball has passed beyond the net.

questions.question: A player may complete an attack hit on the opponent's serve when the ball is in the front zone and entirely above the top of the net.
questions.explanation: No player may complete an attack hit on the opponent's serve when the ball is in the front zone and entirely higher than the top of the net.

questions.question: A serious accident happens while the ball is in play. What should happen?
options: Play continues until the rally ends
The referee stops play immediately and the rally is replayed
Only the captain may stop play
The injured team loses the rally
questions.explanation: If a serious accident occurs while the ball is in play, the referee stops the game immediately, allows medical help, and the rally is replayed.

questions.question: If an injured or ill player cannot be replaced legally or exceptionally, that player may receive one 3-minute recovery time in the match.
questions.explanation: A player who cannot be replaced legally or exceptionally may be given one 3-minute recovery time in the match.

questions.question: In an exceptional substitution, who may replace the injured or ill player?
options: Any player not on the court, except a libero, the second libero, or their regular replacement player
questions.explanation: An exceptional substitution may use any player who is not on the court at that moment, except a libero, the second libero, or their regular replacement player.

questions.question: An exceptional substitution counts as one of the team's regular substitutions.
questions.explanation: An exceptional substitution is not counted as a regular substitution.

questions.question: The first delay by a team in a match is a delay warning.
questions.explanation: The first delay in the match by a team member is sanctioned with a delay warning.

questions.question: What is the usual result of the second delay by the same team in the match?
options: Only a warning is given again
Point and service to the opponent
questions.explanation: The second and later delays by the same team in the same match are delay penalties: point and service to the opponent.

questions.question: If a team has only one libero and that libero becomes unable to play, the coach may redesignate another player who is not on the court at that moment, except the regular replacement player.
questions.explanation: When a team has only one libero available, the coach may redesignate any other player not on court at that moment, except the regular replacement player.

questions.question: If a team has two liberos and one becomes unable to play, the team may continue with one libero.
questions.explanation: When a team has two liberos and one becomes unable to play, the team may continue the match with the remaining libero.

questions.question: A yellow card by itself is a warning, not a sanction.
questions.explanation: A yellow card alone is a formal warning. It is not a sanction and has no immediate scoring consequence.

questions.question: The first offensive conduct by a team member results in expulsion.
questions.explanation: The first offensive conduct by a team member is sanctioned by expulsion.

questions.question: After the line-up sheet has been given to the 2nd referee or scorer, the starting line-up cannot be changed without a regular substitution.
questions.explanation: Once the line-up sheet has been delivered, changes to the line-up must be made through a regular substitution.

questions.question: Before the set starts, if players are standing in the wrong positions compared with the line-up sheet, their positions are corrected with no sanction.
questions.explanation: If the discrepancy is found before the set starts, the players are placed correctly according to the line-up sheet and there is no sanction.

questions.question: Before the set starts, if a player on court is not listed on the line-up sheet for that set, the player must be changed to match the line-up sheet, with no sanction.
questions.explanation: If an unlisted player is found on court before the set starts, that player must be changed so the line-up matches, and there is no sanction.

questions.question: What determines a team's rotational order throughout the set?
questions.explanation: The team's starting line-up sets the rotational order, and that order must be maintained throughout the set.

questions.question: If the wrong player serves, the team has committed a rotational fault.
questions.explanation: A rotational fault happens when the service is not made according to the rotational order.

questions.question: A team can be in correct overlap positions and still commit a rotational fault if the wrong player serves.
questions.explanation: Overlap order and service order are different checks. A team may be positioned correctly and still have a rotational fault if the wrong server serves.

questions.question: A rotational fault caught only after the rally ends gives the opponent one point, even if the faulting team won that rally.
questions.explanation: If the rotational fault is found only after the rally has finished, only one point is awarded to the opponent, regardless of the rally result.

questions.question: If the exact moment of a rotational fault cannot be determined, no earlier points are cancelled.
questions.explanation: When the exact moment of the rotational fault cannot be determined, there is no points cancellation.

questions.question: If a line-up discrepancy is found later in the set, the opponent's points remain valid.
questions.explanation: When a line-up discrepancy is found later, the opponent's points remain valid.

questions.question: If a line-up discrepancy is found later in the set, the opponent also receives a point and the next service.
questions.explanation: When a later line-up discrepancy is discovered, the opponent receives a point and the next service, and the faulty team must return to the correct positions.
